questions.question: Why should a recommendation service retrieve hundreds of candidates but rank only a smaller pool with the richest model?
options: Retrieval preserves recall across a large catalog while bounded ranking protects latency and compute
The rich ranker cannot use user or item features
Every retrieved item must appear in the final slate
Candidate generation is always more accurate than ranking
questions.explanation: Retrieval cheaply narrows a huge catalog with a recall objective. Rich cross-feature scoring is reserved for a bounded pool so it can improve precision without violating the online deadline.

questions.question: At 15,000 recommendation requests per second and 100 ranked candidates per request, how many candidate scores are computed each second?
options: 1.5 million
15 million
150 million
questions.explanation: 15,000 requests/s x 100 candidates/request equals 1,500,000 candidate scores/s. This quantity drives ranker and feature-serving capacity.

questions.question: Where should inventory and policy eligibility be enforced when candidate caches may be stale?
options: Only during nightly model training
Only when candidates first enter the cache
Immediately before final slate release, in addition to earlier filtering
After the user clicks an item
questions.explanation: Earlier filtering saves work, but final policy must consult sufficiently fresh authoritative state. A stale candidate or fallback must not reintroduce an ineligible item.

questions.question: Which logged field is essential for correcting position and exposure bias in training data?
options: Only the items that were purchased
The full catalog snapshot from the previous year
The final invoice number
Which items were shown, their positions, and the policy or experiment that selected them
questions.explanation: Outcomes are interpretable only relative to exposure. Impression, position, policy, and experiment lineage reveal what the user had an opportunity to choose.

questions.question: A new ranker improves offline NDCG but increases returns and reduces 30-day retention in a canary. What should happen?
options: Promote it because offline ranking quality is the only release gate
Stop or roll back the canary and investigate the objective, slices, and feedback data
Remove return and retention metrics from the dashboard
Increase traffic immediately to collect more purchases
questions.explanation: Offline relevance is diagnostic evidence, not the product objective. Online business and long-term guardrails can veto a model whose proxy metric improved.

questions.question: The personalized feature service is unavailable. Which fallback preserves the lesson's invariant?
options: Serve unchecked cached personalized slates indefinitely
Bypass inventory filters so the slate is never empty
Serve regional or category-popular items after fresh eligibility and deduplication checks
Retry every dependency without a deadline
questions.explanation: Eligible popularity is a useful degraded mode because it removes personalization while preserving policy. The system should expose and monitor the fallback rather than bypass correctness.
